title: Polyglot Bootstraps: ergonomic streaming adapters, retry patterns, and starter app cookbooks
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Create a set of opinionated, ergonomic starter templates and cookbook snippets for Next.js, FastAPI, Go HTTP servers and a CLI that demonstrate best-practice SDK usage: streaming adapters (browser/web and Node), safe retry patterns with jittered backoff, cancellation and graceful shutdown, token accounting, and integration tests. Aim for lightweight copy-paste examples that teams can adopt as-is and that show Redwood-specific recommendations (batching-friendly prompts, KV-cache hinting headers, model tolerance profile notes).
tasks: 1) Design ergonomic streaming primitives for each language (TransformStream/AsyncIterator for TS, async generator + httpx for Python, channel-based streaming for Go). 2) Implement starter apps: Next.js streaming demo page, FastAPI streaming endpoint sample, Go HTTP server example with graceful shutdown and client wrapper, and a simple CLI (rwdctl-like) showing stream tailing and retries. 3) Add cookbook snippets: exponential-backoff with full-jitter, idempotency keys, prefix caching hints, streaming to file and terminal, and robust test harnesses (integration + e2e mocks). 4) Review with DX and Docs for copy clarity. 5) Publish packages/examples repo and link in SDK docs.
acceptance_criteria:
- Each starter repo builds and runs locally with documented steps.
- Streaming examples provide both raw chunk and structured event patterns and demonstrate cancellation.
- Retry helpers with full-jitter backoff present in each language and used in examples; default retrypolicy is safe for idempotent generation requests.
- CI includes integration tests using local dev server and a mocked Redwood runtime; tests validate retry paths, stream concat behavior, and graceful shutdown.
- Docs page with code snippets and a short TL;DR for production migration guidance.
comments: 2026-03-05 Aisha Patel: Kickoff — scoped to four starter archetypes (Next.js, FastAPI, Go HTTP server, CLI). Focus on developer ergonomics first, then performance additions (batching headers).
